PENA Vice Governor and Presiding Officer DILG Legafpi2 20fff.2011 MEMBERS OF THE SANGGUNIANG PANLALAWIGAN Province of Camarines Sur Legislative Building, Provincial Capitol Complex Cadlan, Pili, Camarines Sur Gentlemen/Mesdames: QECORCS secti0N RELEASED DAW: This has reference to your 05 September 2011 Resolution Nos. 404 and 407 requesting the undersigned's clarification/opinion on whether or not House Bill No. 4820 ( "An Act Creating the Province of Nueva Camarines', particularly Section 12 thereof, is an amendment to the long-time practice in the apportionment/allocation of regular members in the Sanggunian of first class provinces, and singularly applicable to the new province of Nueva Camarines and/or the province of Camarines Sur, when the House of Representatives allocated only six (6) and nine (9) members, respectively, in the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. Please note that HB 4820, the charter of Nueva Camarines, shall specifically govern its creation and other matters necessary for its existence as a political body corporate. This is without prejudice to the provisions of law, specifically the Local Government Code (LGC), which shall continue to govern the determination of the number of members in the sangguniang panlalawigan, among other matters. Amendments to the LGC should embrace only one subject which should be expressed in the title of the bill following Section 26 (I), Article VI of the 1987 Constitution. The Province of Camarines Sur is presently classified as a first class province. Under Section 41 (b) of the LGC and Article 94 (3) of its IRR, the sangguniang panlalawigan of a first class province shall have ten (IO) regular/elective members. Notably under Section 8 of the LGC, the division of an existing local government unit shall not reduce the income, population, or land area of the local government unit or units concerned to less than the minimum requirements prescribed under Section 7 of the LGC. In addition, the income classification of the original local government unit or units shall not fall below its current income classification prior to such division. Clearly, the income classification of the Province of Camarines Sur should not fall below the income range set by the Department of Finance (DOF) for first class provinces. In effect, the Province of Camarines Sur's Sangguniang Panlalawigan shall have ten (IO) regular/elective members. On the other hand, once HB 4820 is approved by a majority of votes cast in a plebiscite, the new province of Nueva Camarines shall be classified by the Bureau of Local Government Finance (BLGF) based on its annual income. Pending its classification, membership in its sangguniang panlalawigan shall be three (3) members per district, as provided under section 12 of HB 4820. We hope the foregoing sufficiently addresses your concern. Very truly yours, A . JESU B. D Director III
